page: Microsoft Azure B4as_v2 is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing a burstable CPU allocation model on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, accompanied by 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). The underlying x86_64 architecture features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, including instruction support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput typical of burstable instances. The instance registers a strong single-core stress-ng metric (2702.19) and a standard Geekbench single-core score of 1525.0. Conversely, sustained parallel execution reveals limitations, indicated by bottom-tier results in stress-ng multi-core (5400.28), Geekbench multi-core (3416.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (21.68 GB/sec). Memory subsystems operate in the middle tier, yielding 67.42 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 47.04 GB/sec for uncached write transfers.

Network serving and in-memory transactional tests similarly illustrate low parallel density, recording 4.18 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 4.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. From an operational perspective, the B4as_v2 represents an economical resource tier for non-sustained compute profiles, trading off continuous maximum compute power for balanced memory density. It is functionally suited for development environments, low-traffic web applications, non-critical build servers, and intermittent background processing tasks that benefit from transient CPU bursts.
description: Microsoft Azure B4as_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz and paired with 16.0 GB of RAM. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 instance provides robust single-core metrics—such as 2702.19 on stress-ng single-core—alongside standard memory transfer speeds reaching 67.42 GB/sec on uncached reads. However, its burstable allocation limits continuous parallel capacity, evidenced by lower-tier rankings in multi-core Geekbench and bzip3 decompression tests. The instance features no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on external storage capabilities. This hardware configuration offers a cost-effective operational profile for variable workloads, making it well matched for dev/test servers, small code compilation jobs, low-traffic web hosting, and batch processing tasks with intermittent compute requirements.
